question: Show me how to take Punctual Pros nationwide
html:
Taking Punctual Pros nationwide

Follow the Smith + Howard growth plan: fill in the Central-PA core, repeat the Horvath deal across neighbouring states, build a Mid-Atlantic hub, then consolidate the One Hour / Benjamin Franklin / Mister Sparky system. Integrate each step before adding the next. Smith + Howard went from ~100 professionals to ~800 and ~4x revenue in about 3.7 years before its sale to TPG Growth (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Starting point

  • ~$22M est. FY2025 revenue, 25 Authority Brands territories, 248 core zips with ~1.0M housing units (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • One out-of-state add-on so far: Horvath, Jersey Shore.
  • Current run-rate is est. ~$24M revenue, ~$2.9M EBITDA, 85 technicians and 6,500 members.

Four phases

PhaseMonthsFocusEnd-state (est.)
10–12Core plus 261 nearby zips (176 PA, 85 MD); 1–2 tuck-ins$38M rev, $5.3M EBITDA, 32 territories
29–24Repeat the Horvath deal in PA, NJ, MD, DE, southern NY (54 unowned territories)$65M rev, $9.8M EBITDA, 44 territories
318–36I-81/I-95 hub: Baltimore-DC, Richmond, Philadelphia suburbs, Pittsburgh$100M rev, $16M EBITDA, 58 territories
4LaterNational consolidator in a 1,066-outlet, $831M system (~2.3% held today)Not modelled

All roadmap figures are assumptions (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

First targets

Top-ranked fits from the 61-company screen (Punctual Pros add-on targets):

  • Lancaster Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electrical (84). Four trades, 5 miles from HQ.
  • Ron Williams group, West Chester tri-brand (82). The same owner also runs Delmarva.
  • C&C Air Conditioning (82). ~65 employees, Jersey Shore.
  • Zimmerman (80) and PHE South Jersey (80).

Revenue and headcount are mostly missing because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable. Diligence data is needed before sizing any deal.

What winners did

From 17 sponsor case studies (Home-services company case studies):

  • Hire an integrator early. TurnPoint, Wrench and Apex all did.
  • Add about one company a quarter, then accelerate.
  • Run every brand on one system. Authority Brands has used ServiceTitan since 2024.
  • Build memberships. Champions grew from ~60,000 to ~150,000 members and sold at a reported ~18.5x.
  • Own the technician pipeline through academies.
  • Avoid the failure pattern. Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them.

Operating leverage

  • The website is only the front door. The plan's real lever is AI (Punctual Pros nationwide plan):
  • a 24/7 voice dispatcher (ServiceTitan reports 70% booking);
  • missed-call text-back;
  • AI estimating.
  • The roadmap assumes a shared contact center lifts margin from ~12% to ~16% (est.).
  • Competition is real. 17 PE sponsors chase the same founders.

Next actions

  1. Recruit an integrator COO before closing the Phase 1 tuck-ins.
  2. Open founder conversations with Lancaster Plumbing and the Ron Williams group. Request financials to fill the revenue gaps.
  3. Pilot the AI voice dispatcher in the core territories. Track booking rate against the current baseline.
  4. Set a membership-per-technician target, using Champions' ~83 as the benchmark.

Integrate each step before adding the next. Smith + Howard went from ~100 professionals to ~800 and ~4x revenue in about 3.7 years before its sale to TPG Growth (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## Starting point

- ~$22M est. FY2025 revenue, 25 Authority Brands territories, 248 core zips with ~1.0M housing units (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- One out-of-state add-on so far: Horvath, Jersey Shore.
- Current run-rate is est. ~$24M revenue, ~$2.9M EBITDA, 85 technicians and 6,500 members.

## Four phases

| Phase | Months | Focus | End-state (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–12 | Core plus 261 nearby zips (176 PA, 85 MD); 1–2 tuck-ins | $38M rev, $5.3M EBITDA, 32 territories |
| 2 | 9–24 | Repeat the Horvath deal in PA, NJ, MD, DE, southern NY (54 unowned territories) | $65M rev, $9.8M EBITDA, 44 territories |
| 3 | 18–36 | I-81/I-95 hub: Baltimore-DC, Richmond, Philadelphia suburbs, Pittsburgh | $100M rev, $16M EBITDA, 58 territories |
| 4 | Later | National consolidator in a 1,066-outlet, $831M system (~2.3% held today) | Not modelled |

All roadmap figures are assumptions (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## First targets

Top-ranked fits from the 61-company screen (Punctual Pros add-on targets):
- Lancaster Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electrical (84). Four trades, 5 miles from HQ.
- Ron Williams group, West Chester tri-brand (82). The same owner also runs Delmarva.
- C&C Air Conditioning (82). ~65 employees, Jersey Shore.
- Zimmerman (80) and PHE South Jersey (80).

Revenue and headcount are mostly missing because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable. Diligence data is needed before sizing any deal.

## What winners did

From 17 sponsor case studies (Home-services company case studies):
- Hire an integrator early. TurnPoint, Wrench and Apex all did.
- Add about one company a quarter, then accelerate.
- Run every brand on one system. Authority Brands has used ServiceTitan since 2024.

- Own the technician pipeline through academies.
- Avoid the failure pattern. Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them.

## Operating leverage

- The website is only the front door. The plan's real lever is AI (Punctual Pros nationwide plan):
  - a 24/7 voice dispatcher (ServiceTitan reports 70% booking);
  - missed-call text-back;
  - AI estimating.
- The roadmap assumes a shared contact center lifts margin from ~12% to ~16% (est.).
- Competition is real. 17 PE sponsors chase the same founders.

## Next actions

1. Recruit an integrator COO before closing the Phase 1 tuck-ins.
2. Open founder conversations with Lancaster Plumbing and the Ron Williams group. Request financials to fill the revenue gaps.
3. Pilot the AI voice dispatcher in the core territories. Track booking rate against the current baseline.
